headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection/data-flow coupling: Khoj can ingest and expose indexed notes, while LightZero is read-only and isolated, so most pairwise hazards are limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj can read indexed files and supports RAG/web-search style ingestion, so malicious content in notes could influence its outputs. LightZero has no input surfaces or ingestion path, so it is not a meaningful injection target. The pair lacks a shared channel by default, making this a small, manual-bridge risk.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies Khoj output into LightZero prompts or configs
IF shared notes contain attacker-controlled instructions
mitigations: Review copied text before reuse
Keep LightZero prompts separate from Khoj notes
Disable web search in Khoj for untrusted corpora
Tag untrusted documents in the index
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to retrieved snippets

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents and has broad network egress, so sensitive content can leave the local workspace through its backend or configured search providers. LightZero touches no data classes and has no egress, so it is not the leakage source. The pair risk is driven by Khoj’s default data handling, not by LightZero.
conditions: IF Khoj is configured with external search providers or cloud inference
IF indexed notes include sensitive personal data
mitigations: Use self-hosted Khoj only
Remove sensitive notes from the index
Audit configured search providers
Rotate any model API keys
requires-engineering: enforce per-document redaction before indexing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj can read the filesystem but cannot write it, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses; LightZero also cannot write, modify git, or use the filesystem. With no overlapping write surface, there is no plausible capability conflict between the pair.
conditions: IF either profile gains filesystem write or git mutation capability
mitigations: Keep both agents in read-only mode
Do not mount a shared writable workspace
requires-engineering: add OS-level write sandboxing

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can generate retrieved answers from notes, but LightZero is a game-playing library with no documented downstream action-taking or input ingestion path. Without a consumer that treats Khoj output as authoritative, the cascade is limited to manual misuse rather than an automated harmful chain.
conditions: IF a human copies Khoj-generated claims into LightZero training or configuration
IF LightZero is wrapped by an external orchestrator that acts on Khoj output
mitigations: Verify Khoj outputs before reuse
Keep LightZero configs under separate review
Avoid auto-feeding retrieval answers into code or training data
requires-engineering: add validation gates before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj processes personal notes and indexed documents, which can create residency or retention obligations, while LightZero touches no regulated data classes and has no stated compliance surface. The pair itself does not create a documented mismatch, but Khoj’s handling of personal data warrants basic policy review.
conditions: IF personal notes include regulated personal data
IF Khoj is deployed under a retention policy different from the source data policy
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for Khoj
Exclude regulated data from indexing
Document data residency for the deployment
Review deletion/export procedures
requires-engineering: add policy-based data classification controls
